type: color (pH dependent, Red, green and purple ranges)

more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Anthocyanins are a group of pigments extracted from edible fruit or vegetables; preparations may contain several different pigment structures and their glycosides. It is used to add colour or restore colour lost during food manufacture. Extracted from edible fruits or vegetables using permitted water-based or solvent processes. The extract is concentrated and may be dried. The specified material is supplied as red powder or liquid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Extracted from edible fruits or vegetables using permitted water-based or solvent processes. The extract is concentrated and may be dried.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA considered assessed aqueous grape-skin and blackcurrant extracts unlikely to raise concern at reported food-use levels.
Other sources or extraction methods lacked sufficient characterisation for the same conclusion in 2013.
